stories.headline: China imposes export controls on tunnel-boring machines sought by India, cites ‘national security’
stories.title: China imposes export controls on tunnel-boring machines sought by India, cites ‘national security’
stories.summary: Announcement comes days after Beijing announced plans to impose export controls on 40 cutting-edge technologies, including those for advanced solar manufacturing, AI platforms
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in title weight 70
article_sentences: China on Monday said it would introduce export controls on tunnel-boring machines “to better safeguard national security and interests”, starting November 18.
India has already been facing difficulties in customs clearance and delays in importing TBMs from China for several critical infrastructure projects.

The latest announcement comes days after Beijing announced a plan to impose sweeping export controls on 40 cutting-edge technologies, including those for certain advanced solar manufacturing and some AI platforms.

The Chinese Commerce Ministry said on Monday in an announcement it was “introducing export controls on tunnel-boring machines and related items and optimising and adjusting export-control measures for certain dredgers and related items.” The measures will take effect on November 18.
The ministry said prior to the announcement, China had “notified the relevant countries and regions with which it has established export-control dialogue mechanisms.”
“The items covered by these measures have clear dual-use (civilian and military) characteristics,” the announcement said.

“The measures are intended to better safeguard national security and interests, while also enabling China to better fulfil its international obligations, including those related to non-proliferation”.

India has previously raised with China the delays in customs clearance for imports of TBMs, which are used in India for several critical projects including the construction of metro rail networks in cities, railway corridors and key tunnelling projects, including in border areas.
India is dependent on imports for the machines.
Difficulties in imports from China started in 2024.

In October of that year, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal had publicly raised the issue with visiting German Vice Chancellor Robert Habeck, pointing out that China was blocking the export of TBMs made by a German company in China.
On Monday, China also announced export control measures related to certain types of drones.

stories.headline: Flood Of Pleas By Employees Challenging Their Transfers Has Paralysed Govt Functioning: Rajasthan High Court
stories.title: Flood Of Pleas By Employees Challenging Their Transfers Has Paralysed Govt Functioning: Rajasthan High Court
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: While hearing a bunch of petitions by government employees, challenging their transfer orders, Rajasthan High Court observed that the government functioning was paralysed since most of the employees were not willing to join the transferred place of posting.
The bench of Justice Anoop Kumar Dhand further opined that maximum number of employees were approaching the Court for getting the transfer orders cancelled.
It was held that the jurisdiction of the Court under Article 226, is not to act as a second appellate authority over the transfer orders passed by the competent authority or the appellate tribunal.

“This Court is constrained to observe that there is a flood of writ petitions assailing the transfer orders…Maximum number of employees are approaching this Court and the Rajasthan Civil Services Appellate Tribunal (for short, 'the Tribunal') for getting their transfer orders stayed and cancelled on one pretext or the other, thereby bringing the administrative machinery to a standstill.”
4) In extreme case of hardship to life threatening disease effecting the service conditions.
“It is settled proposition of law that transfer is an incidence of service.
No employee has a vested right to remain posted at a particular place of his choice.

It is for the employer or the competent authority to decide as to where and how its employees are to be posted, considering the administrative exigencies, public interest and smooth functioning of the administration.”

While opining that no other ground could be valid for interfering in transfer orders, including personal inconveniences, hardship, long stay, etc., the Court held that no ground for interference was present in the present batch of petitions.

However, in order to balance equities, the Court granted liberty to the petitioners to file representations before competent authorities within 2 weeks, and directed the authorities to decide the same within further 2 weeks.
Accordingly, the transfer orders were stayed for 4 weeks.

stories.title: Chennai rains: Flash flood risk, IMD alert
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Heavy rainfall is expected to continue across Tamil Nadu, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warning of heavy to very heavy showers, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds in several districts.
Schools in Chennai and neighbouring districts have been declared closed on Wednesday, October 21, following heavy overnight rainfall.

The IMD has forecast continued heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places in Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40-50 kmph at one or two places.
Several other districts are also likely to receive heavy rain, with residents advised to monitor weather alerts and take precautions amid the possibility of localised flooding.
Schools in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram and Ranipet have been declared closed on Wednesday, October 21, following heavy rainfall, according to local media reports.
District administrations announced the holiday in view of the prevailing weather conditions.
The closures come as the IMD forecasts further rainfall across Tamil Nadu.
Parents and students should check announcements from their respective district administrations and schools for any further updates.
Southern Tamil Nadu: Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari may receive heavy to very heavy rainfall at isolated places.
Western Tamil Nadu: The Nilgiris, Coimbatore, Erode and Tiruppur are likely to experience heavy rain.
Central and interior districts: Namakkal, Karur, Theni, Dindigul, Madurai, Tenkasi and Virudhunagar are also under the heavy rainfall forecast.
Delta and coastal districts: Pudukkottai, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam and Mayiladuthurai may receive heavy showers.

stories.headline: Third Chair: Who Should Pick India's Election Commissioners
stories.title: Third Chair: Who Should Pick India's Election Commissioners
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: On 23 September, a two-judge Bench of the Supreme Court split on whether the challenge to the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 needs a Constitution Bench.
Justice Dipankar Datta held that Anoop Baranwal.
Union of India, had already settled the governing principles and that the Court needed only to test the 2023 law against them.

Justice Satish Chandra Sharma held that the question of whether Parliament could exclude a neutral selector from the appointment committee was a substantial question of constitutional interpretation arising for the first time, and that Article 145(3) reserves such questions for a larger Bench.
Both judges agreed that the papers should go to Chief Justice Surya Kant.
The question before the larger Bench is narrower than the political debate suggests, and harder.
It is not a question of whether Parliament could legislate.

Article 324(2) makes appointments by the President “subject to the provisions of any law made in that behalf by Parliament”, and the 2023 Constitution Bench said its own committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition, and the Chief Justice would hold good only until such a law was made.
At the hearing on reference, the Solicitor General argued that Anoop Baranwal prescribed an interim arrangement, not a constitutional requirement that the Chief Justice sit on the committee.
Justice Datta appears to accept part of that: had the Constitution Bench meant the Chief Justice's presence to be binding, he observed, it would have said so.
The live question is different.
It is whether the law Parliament actually made meets the standard of independence that Article 324 carries within it, and that Anoop Baranwal articulated.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear Pinarayi Vijayan's plea in CMRL case
stories.title: Supreme Court to hear Pinarayi Vijayan's plea in CMRL case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: On October 15, Kerala HC rejected applications of Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and her husband P. A Mohammed Riyas to file an appeal against the single judge's October 9 order.

According to the Supreme Court website, the special bench, which will be sitting at the time when the apex court is closed for the Dussehra holidays, is scheduled to consider the petitions filed by Pinarayi Vijayan and his kin against the high court order dismissing their pleas to file appeals against a single judge's direction to lodge an FIR against them in the alleged Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) bribery case.

On October 15, the Kerala High Court rejected the applications of Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and her husband P. A Mohammed Riyas to file an appeal against the single judge's October 9 order, while holding that "an accused in a corruption case has no legal right to be heard before registering the FIR."
Vijayan, Veena and Riyas, in their appeals before the high court, had claimed that they were not heard by the single judge before issuing the October 9 direction to lodge the FIR.

They further claimed before the high court that the petition, in which the single judge passed the October 9 order, was in the form of a public interest litigation (PIL) and therefore, it should have been heard by a division bench which deals with PILs.

The appeals before the high court were moved in the wake of the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau's (VACB) Special Investigation Unit-1 registering two FIRs against Vijayan and his family members in connection with the alleged CMRL bribery case.
The Kerala High Court on October 9 directed the VACB to register a case based on a report submitted by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the state police.
The ED had sought registration of a case based on evidence gathered during its investigation and searches conducted under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.

stories.headline: IMD update: More rain in store for Tamil Nadu as low-pressure area brews
stories.title: IMD update: More rain in store for Tamil Nadu as low-pressure area brews
stories.summary: India Meteorological Department predicts very heavy showers over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal even as a second ‘low’ could intensify into a major system over the Bay early next week
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The north-east monsoon continues to be in a vigorous state over the South Peninsula, with isolated very heavy rainfall of 11.5–20 cm forecast over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on Wednesday and Thursday as a cyclonic circulation over the south-west Bay of Bengal and adjoining Tamil Nadu coast prepares to consolidate into a low-pressure area by this (Wednesday) afternoon.

The developing system is expected to sustain an active spell of rain over the region, while an elongated trough of lower pressure extending from the circulation towards north coastal Andhra Pradesh is helping organise clouds and showers across a broad swathe of the southern peninsula.
Chennai can expect a largely overcast day, with rain and thunderstorms giving way to a brief lull before showers return around 10 pm.
The skies are likely to clear again by Thursday morning.
Bengaluru, meanwhile, may remain partly cloudy, with possibility of thunderstorms between 3 pm and 8 pm before conditions improve.
Sunny intervals between showers, coupled with October’s lingering heat, keep humidity levels uncomfortably high.
India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast isolated heavy rainfall of 6–11 cm over Kerala and Mahe for seven days from Wednesday, and over South Interior Karnataka for four days.
Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to receive isolated heavy showers for another four days from Friday, while Lakshadweep could see similar rainfall for five days from Thursday.
Coastal Karnataka is in line for isolated heavy rain on Saturday, with Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema also under the heavy-rain watch on Wednesday.
The morning cloudscape offered a glimpse of the system’s reach.
At 9.15 am, a dense band of rain-bearing clouds stretched southwards from Kavali along the Andhra coast through Nellore and Gudur, extending inland towards Tirupati, Nagari and Chittoor.
The belt covered parts of Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema, with isolated to scattered rainfall, thunderstorms and lightning likely at several places.
